nodes.summary:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be finite measures on $\mathbb{R}$ that give no mass to the complement of an interval $[a, b]$. If $\int x^k \, d\mu = \int x^k \, d
u$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, then $\mu = 
u$.
nodes.title: Compactly supported measures are determined by their moments

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb{R}$, let $R > 0$ and $C \in \mathbb{R}$, and suppose that $x \mapsto x^{2k}$ is $\mu$-integrable with $\int x^{2k} \, d\mu \le C R^{2k}$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $\mu(\{x : |x| > R\}) = 0$.
nodes.title: Moment bounds confine the support
